refined_requirements.text: Students, professors, and academic administrators are specialized roles of a university user.
An authenticated identity and role are required before performing any protected operation.
A university user shall search published course offerings and inspect their course, section, instructor, meeting schedule, capacity, and remainingâseat information.
A student shall register for a selected course offering during its registration period and receive the result.
A student shall atomically swap a current registration for another course offering and receive the result.

Before accepting a registration or a swap, the system shall perform mandatory enrollmentâeligibility validation including registrationâperiod, duplicateâenrollment, capacity, and timetableâconflict checks.
A student shall view current registrations and the resulting class schedule.
A student shall drop a selected registration during the allowed period and receive the result.

While viewing the current class schedule, a student may optionally export it in a downloadable format using the information already presented; the schedule view remains complete without performing the export.
When a registration is rejected only because an offering is full and its waitlist is enabled, the student may join the waitlist; the rejected registration remains a complete result without joining.
A student shall view and cancel their own waitlist entries.
A professor shall review assigned course offerings and their current student rosters.
An academic administrator shall create and update academic terms and their registration periods.
An academic administrator shall create, update, publish, or cancel course offerings and assign their instructor, meeting schedule, and enrollment capacity.
The system shall authorize each protected operation according to the authenticated universityâuser role.
Course, offering, term, universityâuser, registration, and waitlist information shall survive application and server restarts.
Concurrent registration, swap, drop, and waitlist operations shall preserve enrollment capacity, registration uniqueness, and waitlist ordering.
The pilot service shall be deployed in the AWS Seoul Region (apânortheastâ2).
The monthly cloud budget for the pilot shall not exceed 500â¯USD.
The pilot shall run on Docker containers on Linux virtual machines provisioned with Terraform.
Managed database services, Kubernetes, and serverless compute are prohibited for the pilot.
The pilot shall use synthetic data instead of real personal data.
HTTPS, TLS certificates, and domain management are outside the scope of the pilot.
Recovery from a dataâstorage server failure is not required for the pilot.

actors.name: UniversityUser
actors.description: A generic university user that must be authenticated before any protected operation. Serves as the parent role for all specialized universityâuser types.

actors.name: Student
actors.description: A university user who can search course offerings, register for courses, swap registrations, view and export schedules, drop courses, and manage waitâlist entries.

actors.name: Professor
actors.description: A university user who reviews the course offerings assigned to them and inspects the current student rosters for those offerings.

actors.name: AcademicAdministrator
actors.description: A university user responsible for creating and updating academic terms, registration periods, and course offerings (including publishing, cancelling, assigning instructors, schedules, and capacities).

use_cases.goal: Search published course offerings and inspect their course, section, instructor, meeting schedule, capacity, and remainingâseat information.

use_cases.name: Register for a course offering
use_cases.goal: Register for a selected course offering during its registration period and receive the result.

use_cases.name: Swap registration for another course offering
use_cases.goal: Atomically swap a current registration for another course offering and receive the result.

use_cases.name: View current registrations and class schedule
use_cases.goal: View current registrations and the resulting class schedule.

use_cases.name: Drop a registration
use_cases.goal: Drop a selected registration during the allowed period and receive the result.

use_cases.name: Export class schedule
use_cases.goal: Export the current class schedule in a downloadable format while keeping the schedule view complete.

use_cases.name: Join waitlist for a full offering
use_cases.goal: Join the waitlist for a course offering when registration is rejected because the offering is full and waitlist is enabled.

use_cases.name: Cancel own waitlist entry
use_cases.goal: Cancel a waitlist entry belonging to the student.

use_cases.name: Review assigned course offerings and student rosters
use_cases.goal: Review assigned course offerings and their current student rosters.

use_cases.name: Create and update academic terms and registration periods
use_cases.goal: Create and update academic terms and their registration periods.

use_case_specs.name: Search published course offerings
use_case_specs.trigger: UniversityUser initiates a search for published course offerings

main_scenario.sentence: UniversityUser initiates a search for published course offerings providing search criteria
System retrieves matching published course offerings and presents their course, section, instructor, meeting schedule, capacity, and remaining-seat information
UniversityUser reviews the presented information

extensions.label: 2a
extensions.condition: No published course offerings match the search criteria

handling_steps.sentence: System informs the user that no offerings match the criteria

success_guarantee.sentence: The user receives a list of matching published course offerings, each showing course, section, instructor, meeting schedule, capacity, and remaining-seat information

minimal_guarantee.sentence: If no offerings match, the system informs the user that no offerings match the criteria

use_case_specs.name: Register for a course offering
use_case_specs.trigger: Student initiates registration for a selected course offering.

main_scenario.sentence: Student requests registration for the selected course offering.
System validates registration period, duplicate enrollment, capacity, and timetable conflicts.
System records the registration.
System returns a successful registration result to the student.

handling_steps.sentence: System informs the student that the registration could not be completed and provides the reason.

success_guarantee.sentence: The registration is recorded and the course offering's capacity is not exceeded, each student is enrolled at most once, and wait-list ordering remains unchanged.
The student receives a confirmation of successful registration.

minimal_guarantee.sentence: The student receives a notification that registration failed and the specific validation reason.

use_case_specs.name: Swap registration for another course offering
preconditions: Student has an active registration for a course offering that can be swapped
use_case_specs.trigger: Student requests to swap the active registration for a different course offering

main_scenario.sentence: Student specifies the target course offering to swap into
System validates enrollment eligibility for the target offering, checking registration period, duplicate enrollment, capacity, and timetable conflicts
System atomically removes the current registration and creates a new registration for the target offering
System returns a success result indicating the swap completed

extensions.label: 2a
extensions.condition: validation fails (registration period closed, duplicate enrollment, capacity full, or timetable conflict)

handling_steps.sentence: System informs the student of the validation failure reason

extensions.label: 3a
extensions.condition: concurrent operation changes capacity after validation making the swap impossible

handling_steps.sentence: System aborts the swap, restores the original registration, and informs the student of the concurrency conflict

success_guarantee.sentence: The student's registration for the original offering is replaced by a registration for the target offering, and the system's enrollment data reflect the swap while preserving capacity limits, enrollment uniqueness, and waitlist ordering

minimal_guarantee.sentence: If the swap is not completed, the student's original registration remains unchanged and enrollment data are left as they were before the request

use_case_specs.name: View current registrations and class schedule
use_case_specs.trigger: Student requests to view current registrations and the class schedule.

main_scenario.sentence: Student requests to view current registrations and the class schedule.
System retrieves the student's current registration records.
System derives the class schedule from the retrieved registrations.
System presents the registration list and the schedule to the student.

extensions.label: 2a
extensions.condition: The retrieved registration list is empty

handling_steps.sentence: System informs the student that there are no current registrations and no schedule to display.

success_guarantee.sentence: The student receives an up-to-date list of current registrations together with the corresponding class schedule.

use_case_specs.name: Drop a registration
preconditions: The student is authenticated and authorized to manage registrations.
The allowed drop period for the term is currently active.
The student has an existing registration that is eligible to be dropped.
use_case_specs.trigger: Student initiates a request to drop a selected registration.

main_scenario.sentence: Student selects the registration to be dropped.
System removes the registration from the student's schedule and updates enrollment counts.
System informs the student of the outcome of the drop request.

handling_steps.sentence: System notifies the student that the registration could not be dropped.

success_guarantee.sentence: The registration no longer appears in the student's schedule, enrollment capacity remains within limits, registration uniqueness is preserved, waitlist ordering is unchanged, and the student receives confirmation of the successful drop.

minimal_guarantee.sentence: If the drop cannot be performed, the student receives a result indicating that the registration was not dropped.

finding_keys_before: semantic:spec.no-precondition-recheck:[semantic] remove the redundant period verification step.
finding_keys_after: semantic:spec.no-hidden-branching:[semantic] add an extension that handles the case where the drop cannot be performed, branching from step 2.

finding_keys_before: semantic:spec.no-precondition-recheck:[semantic] remove the redundant period verification step.

use_case_specs.name: Export class schedule
preconditions: Student is viewing the current class schedule.
use_case_specs.trigger: Student requests export of the schedule while viewing it.

main_scenario.sentence: Student requests export of the schedule in a downloadable format.
System generates a downloadable file containing the schedule information currently displayed.
System provides the file to the student for download.

success_guarantee.sentence: The schedule view remains complete and unchanged.
The student receives a downloadable file that reflects the schedule as displayed.

minimal_guarantee.sentence: The schedule view remains complete even if the export is not delivered.

use_case_specs.name: Join waitlist for a full offering
preconditions: The student's registration attempt for the offering was rejected because the offering was full and its waitlist was enabled.
use_case_specs.trigger: Student initiates a request to join the waitlist for the same offering after receiving the rejection.

main_scenario.sentence: Student requests to join the waitlist for the offering.
System confirms that the offering remains full and its waitlist is still enabled.
System records the student on the waitlist preserving the ordering of waitlist entries.
System notifies the student that the waitlist entry was created and provides the current waitlist position.

extensions.label: 2a
extensions.condition: the offering now has available seats or its waitlist is disabled

handling_steps.sentence: System informs the student that seats are available (or the waitlist is disabled) and suggests registering directly.

success_guarantee.sentence: The original registration attempt remains recorded as a rejected registration without becoming an enrollment.
The student is listed on the waitlist for the offering in the correct order.
Enrollment capacity, registration uniqueness, and waitlist ordering are preserved for the offering.

minimal_guarantee.sentence: If the offering is no longer full or its waitlist is disabled when processed, the system informs the student that a waitlist entry cannot be created and the use case ends without a waitlist entry.

use_case_specs.name: View own waitlist entries
use_case_specs.trigger: Student initiates a request to view their own waitlist entries

main_scenario.sentence: Student requests to view their waitlist entries
System retrieves the student's waitlist entries
System presents the waitlist entries to the student

extensions.label: 2a
extensions.condition: the student has no waitlist entries

handling_steps.sentence: System informs the student that no waitlist entries exist

success_guarantee.sentence: The student sees an up-to-date list of their own waitlist entries

use_case_specs.name: Cancel own waitlist entry
use_case_specs.trigger: Student initiates cancellation of a waitlist entry from their list of waitlist entries

main_scenario.sentence: Student requests cancellation of a specific waitlist entry
System verifies that the waitlist entry belongs to the requesting student
System removes the entry from the waitlist
System confirms the cancellation to the student

extensions.label: 2a
extensions.condition: the specified waitlist entry does not belong to the student or cannot be found

handling_steps.sentence: System informs the student that the waitlist entry cannot be cancelled

success_guarantee.sentence: The waitlist entry is no longer present in the student's waitlist
Waitlist ordering of remaining entries is preserved
Enrollment capacity and registration uniqueness remain unchanged

minimal_guarantee.sentence: If cancellation fails, the student's waitlist remains unchanged

use_case_specs.name: Review assigned course offerings and student rosters
use_case_specs.trigger: Professor initiates a review of the course offerings assigned to them.

main_scenario.sentence: Professor requests the list of course offerings assigned to them.
System provides the list of assigned course offerings.
Professor selects a course offering from the list.
System provides the current student roster for the selected course offering.
Professor reviews the student roster.

success_guarantee.sentence: Professor has obtained and inspected the current student rosters for the selected course offerings.

use_case_specs.name: Create and update academic terms and registration periods
use_case_specs.trigger: AcademicAdministrator initiates a request to create or update an academic term and its registration period.

main_scenario.sentence: AcademicAdministrator provides the term identifier (or indicates a new term) together with registration period dates and other term attributes.
System validates the supplied data for completeness and logical consistency.
System creates a new academic term record or updates the existing term record with the provided registration period and attributes.
System confirms to AcademicAdministrator that the academic term and registration period have been successfully created or updated.

extensions.label: 2a
extensions.condition: supplied data is incomplete or logically inconsistent

handling_steps.sentence: System informs AcademicAdministrator of the validation errors.

success_guarantee.sentence: The academic term and its registration period are stored with the attributes supplied by the AcademicAdministrator.

minimal_guarantee.sentence: No academic term or registration period records are created or modified when the use case aborts.

use_case_specs.name: Manage course offerings
preconditions: AcademicAdministrator is authenticated and authorized to manage course offerings
use_case_specs.trigger: AcademicAdministrator initiates a manage course offering request

main_scenario.sentence: AcademicAdministrator specifies the operation (create, update, publish, cancel, assign instructor, schedule, capacity) and provides the required information for the course offering
System validates the provided information
System performs the requested operation on the course offering
System confirms to AcademicAdministrator that the operation completed successfully

extensions.label: 2a

RR1.text: Students, professors, and academic administrators are specialized roles of a university user.

RR2.text: An authenticated identity and role are required before performing any protected operation.

RR3.text: A university user shall search published course offerings and inspect their course, section, instructor, meeting schedule, capacity, and remainingâseat information.

RR4.text: A student shall register for a selected course offering during its registration period and receive the result.

RR5.text: A student shall atomically swap a current registration for another course offering and receive the result.

RR6.text: Before accepting a registration or a swap, the system shall perform mandatory enrollmentâeligibility validation including registrationâperiod, duplicateâenrollment, capacity, and timetableâconflict checks.

RR7.text: A student shall view current registrations and the resulting class schedule.

RR8.text: A student shall drop a selected registration during the allowed period and receive the result.

RR9.text: While viewing the current class schedule, a student may optionally export it in a downloadable format using the information already presented; the schedule view remains complete without performing the export.

RR10.text: When a registration is rejected only because an offering is full and its waitlist is enabled, the student may join the waitlist; the rejected registration remains a complete result without joining.

RR11.text: A student shall view and cancel their own waitlist entries.

RR12.text: A professor shall review assigned course offerings and their current student rosters.

RR13.text: An academic administrator shall create and update academic terms and their registration periods.

RR14.text: An academic administrator shall create, update, publish, or cancel course offerings and assign their instructor, meeting schedule, and enrollment capacity.

RR15.text: The system shall authorize each protected operation according to the authenticated universityâuser role.

RR16.text: Course, offering, term, universityâuser, registration, and waitlist information shall survive application and server restarts.

RR17.text: Concurrent registration, swap, drop, and waitlist operations shall preserve enrollment capacity, registration uniqueness, and waitlist ordering.

RR18.text: The pilot service shall be deployed in the AWS Seoul Region (apânortheastâ2).

RR19.text: The monthly cloud budget for the pilot shall not exceed 500â¯USD.

RR20.text: The pilot shall run on Docker containers on Linux virtual machines provisioned with Terraform.

RR21.text: Managed database services, Kubernetes, and serverless compute are prohibited for the pilot.

RR22.text: The pilot shall use synthetic data instead of real personal data.

RR23.text: HTTPS, TLS certificates, and domain management are outside the scope of the pilot.

RR24.text: Recovery from a dataâstorage server failure is not required for the pilot.
